comparisons.peer_topic: Data center and cloud computing solutions
comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers a deep portfolio of data center solutions including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, SmartNICs, and FPGAs to meet performance requirements for data centers, supercomputers, and cloud environments.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose the introduction or offering of AI accelerators for data center workloads in 2024. Intel specifically launched the Gaudi 3 AI accelerators, highlighting price-performance advantages for AI inference. Similarly, AMD describes its deep portfolio of data center computing solutions which explicitly includes AI accelerators alongside CPUs and GPUs to meet the computing performance requirements of AI and ML data center environments.

sentences.text: ▪Datacenter AI accelerators and GPUs. In 2024, we launched the Intel® Gaudi® 3 AI accelerators offering significant price-performance advantages for AI inference applications.

We offer a deep portfolio of data center computing solutions including AI accelerators, microprocessors (CPUs), graphic processing units (GPUs), data processing units (DPUs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs), and field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), to meet the vast computing performance requirements of today's data centers, supercomputers, AI and Machine Learning (ML) data center environments and cloud environments.

peer_results.rationale: Broadcom's disclosures focus on VeloRAIN (AI for distributed workload performance/security) and SD-WAN/SASE platforms for distributing AI systems. These topics concern network infrastructure and software-defined networking applications of AI, which is distinct from Intel's specific disclosure of launching hardware AI accelerators (Gaudi 3) for compute workloads.

comparisons.peer_summary: The graphics market is driven by AI, VR/AR, and high-resolution gaming needs; the company announced GDDR7 in 2024, completing its industry-leading portfolio for AI inference on CPUs, NPUs, and GPUs.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address the AI inference market in 2024, though through different hardware components. Intel focuses on its Gaudi 3 AI accelerators for inference applications. Micron focuses on its GDDR7 graphics memory, stating that the addition of GDDR7 completes its product portfolio for AI inference applications on CPUs, NPUs, and GPUs, thereby supporting the broader ecosystem of inference hardware.
